[LSIG.2.6.1] `SeriesBackendIntervalPulse` and `SeriesBackendNumericIntegral` are **load-bearing** DSC atoms: the backing *is* the
aggregation's storage and algorithm, so a runtime that does not recognise the
atom **cannot serve the series**. An unknown `SeriesBackendIntervalPulse`/`SeriesBackendNumericIntegral` at load is therefore a
**hard reject** — the `DS_ERR_DSC_*` version/format-reject path, exactly as
`SeriesBackendRingBuffer` does — **never a skip**: silently skipping it would make an
author-declared series vanish and produce wrong-but-plausible results. This is
the deliberate opposite of the `skip-don't-reject` discipline for
**non-load-bearing** provenance / annotation atoms (the `CallIssued` atom,
[RFCS.15.4]; the `DocString` docstring atom). Registered in [RDSC.7.1].
